_note: Fictional Queensland doctors for the illustrative-profile demonstration (plan §2: 'demonstrate voluntary enrichment using clearly labelled illustrative profiles'). Every record is synthetic: true, realPerson: false, personal.status 'illustrative'. Names were checked against data/providers/*.jsonl name_key on 2026-10-15 and collide with no listed registrant. No publications: a paper is never invented. Loaded by src/data/illustrative.ts behind WATTLE_INCLUDE_ILLUSTRATIVE.

personal.philosophy_of_care: Pelvic pain is real, and I believe you when you describe it. We work together on a plan, and we decide together what the next step is.
personal.why_medicine: I spent my early twenties being told my own pain was normal. I wanted to be the doctor I needed then.
personal.professional_purpose: I want the years between first symptom and diagnosis to be shorter for the next person than they were for me.
personal.communication_approach: I draw the anatomy, use plain language and send you home with a written plan.
personal.lived_experience: I live with endometriosis and had surgery for it twice.
hobbies: Ocean swimming at Burleigh before work
personal.favourite_book_why: It gave me language for how pain and memory sit in the same body.
personal.favourite_podcast_or_music: Conversations with Richard Fidler on the drive in
personal.outside_medicine: Weekends are the dog, the ocean and my sister's kids.

personal.philosophy_of_care: Menopause is a transition, not a disease. I follow the current evidence, explain the options in plain language and you choose.
personal.why_medicine: My mother was a midwife. I grew up with birth stories at the dinner table and never wanted another job.
personal.professional_purpose: I want women in their forties and fifties to get straight answers instead of being told to put up with it.
personal.communication_approach: Frank, unhurried and happy to be questioned.
personal.favourite_book_why: It reminded me that medicine is a story of people being wrong, then slightly less wrong.
personal.favourite_podcast_or_music: Paul Kelly, on repeat since university
personal.outside_medicine: Cooking for too many people on a Sunday.

personal.philosophy_of_care: Pregnancy belongs to the person carrying it. I look at the whole person, ask before I examine, and we decide together.
personal.why_medicine: I was the family translator at my grandmother's appointments. I saw what it costs when nobody explains.
personal.professional_purpose: Culturally safe maternity care for Pasifika families on the Gold Coast, and for anyone who has felt talked over.
personal.communication_approach: I explain before examining and check that you have understood, in English or Samoan.
hobbies: Growing taro in a suburban backyard
personal.favourite_book_why: Four generations of a family carrying each other. That is most of my clinic.
personal.favourite_film: Moana, because my daughters chose it and I stopped minding
personal.favourite_podcast_or_music: Island reggae on the drive home
personal.outside_medicine: Church on Sunday, then a long lunch that goes until dark.

personal.philosophy_of_care: I take time to listen before I reach for a test. Hormones, sleep, movement and mood all belong in the same conversation.
personal.why_medicine: A chemistry teacher told me I asked too many questions. Medicine turned out to be a job where that is the point.
personal.professional_purpose: Fewer women leaving my room with a prescription and no explanation.
personal.communication_approach: Longer appointments, one problem at a time, and nothing decided without you.
personal.favourite_book_why: A doctor learning to be a patient. I reread it most years.
personal.favourite_podcast_or_music: A. R. Rahman while I write letters
personal.outside_medicine: Diwali at my parents' place, which starts in October and ends in December.

personal.philosophy_of_care: I believe you about how hard it is. We work together, at your pace, and the plan is yours as much as mine.
personal.why_medicine: I had a depressive episode in my intern year and a registrar noticed. I wanted to be the one who notices.
personal.professional_purpose: New parents, including fathers, getting help in the first weeks rather than the second year.
personal.communication_approach: Video appointments from your couch, with the baby in frame if that is easier.
personal.lived_experience: I have had depression and still manage it.
hobbies: Fishing from a kayak in Moreton Bay
personal.favourite_book_why: It says the plain things about depression that textbooks skip.
personal.outside_medicine: Two small children and a vegetable patch they keep digging up.

personal.philosophy_of_care: Neurodiversity affirming, strengths based and collaborative. You are the expert on your own brain; I bring the assessment and we decide together.
personal.why_medicine: I was diagnosed with ADHD at thirty-four, during my psychiatry training. Everything before that suddenly made sense.
personal.professional_purpose: Adults who have been called lazy or scattered for decades getting an honest assessment and a plan that fits their life.
personal.communication_approach: Written summaries after every appointment, because I know what it is to forget half of what was said.
personal.lived_experience: I have ADHD, diagnosed as an adult.
personal.favourite_book_why: It changed how I ask questions in an assessment.
personal.outside_medicine: Dumplings with my parents in Sunnybank every second Sunday.

personal.philosophy_of_care: Teenagers can tell when they are being managed rather than heard. I listen first, I am honest with them, and parents are part of the team.
personal.why_medicine: I was a high school teacher before medicine. The students I could not help are why I retrained.
personal.professional_purpose: Young people on the Gold Coast getting seen before a crisis rather than after one.
personal.communication_approach: Plain language, no jargon, and the young person sets the agenda for the first ten minutes.
personal.favourite_book_why: Still the clearest account of a sixteen-year-old nobody is listening to.
personal.favourite_podcast_or_music: Triple J, to keep up with what my patients are listening to
personal.outside_medicine: Camping at Springbrook with no phone reception.

personal.philosophy_of_care: Trauma informed means you set the pace. Nothing happens without your consent, and your culture and faith are part of the room, not left at the door.
personal.why_medicine: My family arrived in Brisbane as refugees when I was nine. The doctor who learned my mother's name is the reason I do this.
personal.professional_purpose: Culturally safe psychiatry for people whose history is hard to tell twice.
personal.communication_approach: Longer first appointments, interpreters when wanted, and I never ask you to retell the worst day on the first visit.
hobbies: Long walks along the river at Kangaroo Point
personal.favourite_book_why: It tells the leaving-home story without pity.
personal.outside_medicine: Cooking for twenty on Fridays and pretending it is effortless.

personal.philosophy_of_care: Chronic fatigue is not deconditioning and it is not in your head. I believe you, we pace together, and the plan changes when your body says so.
personal.why_medicine: I had long COVID in 2022 and spent eight months unable to work. I know what the waiting room feels like from the other chair.
personal.professional_purpose: Longer appointments for people with illnesses that do not fit a fifteen-minute slot.
personal.communication_approach: Forty-minute appointments, email between visits for symptom diaries, and no lectures about exercise.
personal.lived_experience: I had long COVID and still pace my weeks around it.
hobbies: Birdwatching at the Pine Rivers wetlands
personal.favourite_book_why: It taught me patience with things that grow on their own timescale.
personal.favourite_podcast_or_music: Radio National in the car, Nick Cave at home
personal.outside_medicine: A hammock, a book and a border collie who disagrees with the hammock.

personal.philosophy_of_care: Pain is produced by a whole person, not a single joint. I work with you, your physio and your psychologist, and we decide together what a good week looks like.
personal.why_medicine: I trained in anaesthesia and kept meeting people whose pain outlasted the operation. I followed them.
personal.professional_purpose: People with fibromyalgia and hypermobility being taken seriously instead of being told their scans are normal.
personal.communication_approach: Multidisciplinary, unhurried, and I say what I do not know.
hobbies: Pressing flowers from the Mt Coot-tha gardens
personal.favourite_book_why: My grandmother read it to me in Spanish. I still hear her voice in it.
personal.outside_medicine: Learning to sail on the bay and capsizing less each month.

personal.philosophy_of_care: Evidence based and honest. If the research shows something does not work I will say so, and if the research is thin I will say that too.
personal.why_medicine: I liked puzzles with people attached. Rheumatology is the puzzle part of medicine.
personal.professional_purpose: Hypermobile and fibromyalgia patients on the Gold Coast getting a clear diagnosis and a plan, not a shrug.
personal.communication_approach: Straight answers, a written plan and an open door for questions between visits.
hobbies: Knitting jumpers nobody in Queensland needs
personal.favourite_book_why: It is why I show patients the actual numbers.
personal.favourite_podcast_or_music: The Irish Passport, to stay homesick on purpose
personal.outside_medicine: Sunday roasts and arguing about hurling with my dad on the phone.

personal.philosophy_of_care: Gently and without judgement. Dysautonomia and gut symptoms are often dismissed, and I would rather take you seriously and be wrong than the reverse.
personal.why_medicine: My father ran a corner shop and knew every customer's story. I wanted a job like that, with a stethoscope.
personal.professional_purpose: Bulk-billed telehealth for people who are too unwell to sit in a waiting room.
personal.communication_approach: Video or phone, from your bed if that is where today is, and short follow-ups rather than one long slog.
personal.favourite_book_why: It is about everything left unsaid, which is also most consultations.
personal.favourite_podcast_or_music: Old Bollywood soundtracks my mother played
personal.outside_medicine: Bayside walks at Wellington Point when the tide is out.
